From 000eca5d044d1ee23b4ca311793cf3fc528da6c6 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Tianyu Li <tianyu.li@arm.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Jun 2022 17:32:11 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] mm/mempolicy: fix get_nodes out of bound access

When user specified more nodes than supported, get_nodes will access nmask
array out of bounds.

Link: https://lkml.kernel.org/r/20220601093211.2970565-1-tianyu.li@arm.com
Fixes: e130242dc351 ("mm: simplify compat numa syscalls")
Signed-off-by: Tianyu Li <tianyu.li@arm.com>
Cc: Arnd Bergmann <arnd@arndb.de>
Cc: Mark Rutland <mark.rutland@arm.com>
Signed-off-by: Andrew Morton <akpm@linux-foundation.org>

diff --git a/mm/mempolicy.c b/mm/mempolicy.c
index 9689919a2829..f4cd963550c1 100644
--- a/mm/mempolicy.c
+++ b/mm/mempolicy.c
@@ -1388,7 +1388,7 @@ static int get_nodes(nodemask_t *nodes, const unsigned long __user *nmask,
 		unsigned long bits = min_t(unsigned long, maxnode, BITS_PER_LONG);
 		unsigned long t;
 
-		if (get_bitmap(&t, &nmask[maxnode / BITS_PER_LONG], bits))
+		if (get_bitmap(&t, &nmask[(maxnode - 1) / BITS_PER_LONG], bits))
 			return -EFAULT;
 
 		if (maxnode - bits >= MAX_NUMNODES) {
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: mm/mempolicy.c**
- The line of code that accesses the `nmask` array has been modified. 
- The original code accessed `nmask[maxnode / BITS_PER_LONG]`, which could lead to an out-of-bounds access if `maxnode` exceeds the size of the `nmask` array.
- The modified code now accesses `nmask[(maxnode - 1) / BITS_PER_LONG]`, which ensures that the access remains within the bounds of the array.

### Relationships Between Modifications
- The change addresses a bug where the function `get_nodes` could potentially access memory outside the allocated bounds of the `nmask` array when the user specifies more nodes than the system supports. 
- By adjusting the index calculation for the `nmask` array, the patch prevents out-of-bounds access, thereby enhancing the stability and safety of the memory policy management in the kernel. 
- This modification is linked to a previous commit (identified by the hash e130242dc351) that simplified compatibility for NUMA syscalls, indicating that the bug was introduced during that simplification process.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
if (maxnode > PAGE_SIZE*BITS_PER_BYTE)
```
```c
if (get_bitmap(&t, &nmask[maxnode / BITS_PER_LONG], bits))
```
Reason:
The first statement checks if the user-specified `maxnode` exceeds the supported size, but it does not prevent the subsequent access to the `nmask` array. The second statement calculates the index using `maxnode / BITS_PER_LONG`, which can lead to an out-of-bounds access if `maxnode` is greater than the actual number of nodes supported, resulting in potential memory corruption or crashes.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
if (get_bitmap(&t, &nmask[(maxnode - 1) / BITS_PER_LONG], bits))
```
```c
if (maxnode - bits >= MAX_NUMNODES) {
```
Reason:
The first statement modifies the index calculation to `(maxnode - 1) / BITS_PER_LONG`, ensuring that the access to the `nmask` array remains within bounds even when `maxnode` is at its maximum value. The second statement ensures that the logic correctly handles the case where the remaining `maxnode` is still greater than `MAX_NUMNODES`, preventing further out-of-bounds access.
